item.title: Outside 30 Oval Road, London NW1 7DE – Dangerous Trip Hazard Caused by Loose, Uneven and Missing Cobbles, 7th August
item.description:
I would like to report a dangerous trip hazard on the cobbled pavement outside The Henson, 30 Oval Road, London NW1 7DE. The condition of the cobbled paving has significantly deteriorated. There are numerous loose and wobbly cobbles, uneven sections, and several areas where cobbles are completely missing, leaving gaps and holes in the pavement. This has created an unstable walking surface and presents a serious risk of trips and falls. Last night, one of the residents of The Henson tripped over the defective paving, fell to the ground and sustained an injury. This incident highlights the urgent need for the area to be inspected and repaired. This is not an isolated concern. Our night concierge staff have received several complaints from residents, passers-by and tourists about the condition of this pavement. Many people have commented that the cobbled surface is uneven, unstable and difficult to walk on safely. On another occasion, a Tesco delivery driver was pushing a loaded delivery trolley across the area when the uneven surface caused the trolley to become unstable. Several groceries, including bottles of milk and other items, fell onto the ground. I have attached photographs showing some examples of the defects. However, these only represent a small number of affected areas, as there are many more loose, uneven and missing cobbles throughout this section of pavement. As this is a busy pedestrian route used daily by residents, visitors, delivery drivers and members of the public, I am concerned that further accidents may occur if repairs are not carried out promptly. We would be grateful if the area could be inspected and the necessary repairs arranged as soon as possible. Thank you for your attention to this matter.

Nearest road to the pin placed on the map (automatically generated by OpenStreetMap): Oval Road, Chalk Farm, Greater London
Report on FixMyStreet

item.description:

I think they take advantage of the fact the street already looks messy our side, as we have so many recycling bins due to the properties being apartments. If possible can a temporary camera be set up to catch them. I don't want people to think it is me doing this. I find it quite distressing.
